title: Extract-have: lift the two inline haves of big_result into helper1 and helper2
intent: Refactor a monolithic proof of `big_result` whose body holds two inline `have` blocks (30 and 40 lines of tactics) plus a 30-line remainder into two named lemmas `helper1` and `helper2`, each owning one intermediate goal, so the main proof shrinks to a one-line application per lemma plus the remainder.
also_known_as: extract a have as a standalone lemma with context
hoist a have into a lemma

children.name: helper1
children.statement: lemma helper1 (x : α) (hx : Property x) : IntermediateGoal1
children.closed_by: the 30-line tactic block lifted from the inline `have h1 : IntermediateGoal1` (elided in the source as `[30 lines - extracted from h1]`)

children.name: helper2
children.closed_by: the 40-line tactic block lifted from the inline `have h2 : IntermediateGoal2`, using the prior result `h1 : IntermediateGoal1` (elided as `[40 lines - extracted from h2]`)

applicability.goal_shape: A theorem `big_result : Conclusion` whose proof body is a sequence of intermediate goals stated as inline `have`s with long tactic blocks (30-40 lines each), followed by a remainder. The move turns each such `have h : T := by <block>` into a lemma whose conclusion is `T` and whose parameters are exactly the hypotheses the block uses, and the parent's line becomes `have h := helper <args>`.
applicability.use_when: an intermediate `have` is a self-contained statement with local dependencies that is worth testing or reusing on its own, and the parent is long enough (the file says 60-200 lines) that the inline blocks obscure the main argument
applicability.avoid_when: the `have` is short and linear, the helper would need 10+ parameters or its context is too tangled to separate cleanly (the file's 'Bad breakpoints', lines 182-187), or the intermediate result depends on later bindings so it cannot be stated before the parent

claims.claim: The AFTER proof of big_result cites exactly two lemmas, helper1 and helper2, one application each (`have h1 := helper1 x hx`, `have h2 := helper2 x h1`), and these correspond one-to-one to the two inline goals `have h1 : IntermediateGoal1` and `have h2 : IntermediateGoal2` of the BEFORE block.

The main proof drops from the 8-line BEFORE block (lines 192-199), which embeds two elided tactic blocks totalling 70 lines (`[30 lines of tactics...]` + `[40 lines of tactics...]`), to 5 lines of glue (lines 208-212); the two extracted bodies (30 and 40 lines) are moved out into helper1 and helper2.
claims.evidence: counted on the copied file: BEFORE https://github.com/cameronfreer/lean4-skills/blob/3f913c66251b8712bb58e6ce83a453fa96e3f94f/plugins/lean4/skills/lean4/references/proof-refactoring.md#L192-L199 versus AFTER https://github.com/cameronfreer/lean4-skills/blob/3f913c66251b8712bb58e6ce83a453fa96e3f94f/plugins/lean4/skills/lean4/references/proof-refactoring.md#L208-L212

claims.claim: The file states the trigger for this exact move in its own words: refactor when there are 'Large preliminary calculations (50+ line `have` statements)'. This site is the Step 3 illustration of that rule.

The same move is applied again in the file's 'Real Refactoring Example' (lines 295-342): the inline `have hk_bound : ∀ i : Fin (m' + 1), k i < n := by ...` (lines 309-317) is extracted to `private lemma strictMono_all_lt_succ_last` (lines 320-328) and the main proof 'now just calls helper' (line 330).

metrics.how_counted: BEFORE block (lines 192-199) versus AFTER theorem (lines 208-212) of the copied file; the two extracted bodies are stated in the source as 30 and 40 lines of tactics

consequences: Each extracted `have` becomes a top-level lemma whose statement must be exactly the type the parent's `have` expects, with every hypothesis the body uses: helper1 must conclude in IntermediateGoal1 given hx : Property x, and helper2 must take h1 : IntermediateGoal1 — the previous lemma's conclusion — or the glue `have h2 := helper2 x h1` will not elaborate. The file's Step 4 (lines 215-232) turns this into a check: the goal at the old `have` line must match the helper's conclusion. A dropped or mismatched hypothesis breaks sufficiency silently. Sequential dependence is the other cost: helper2 depends on helper1, so the two leaves are not parallelisable as stated (to parallelise, helper2 would re-prove IntermediateGoal1 or take it as an assumption).
